doc.title: Jon Hendricks interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 29, 2000 [interview 2 of 2]

title: Why the churches are finished
summary: Churches as intercessors must go; he recalls the AME church abusing his father.

story.theme_name: Church, faith and religion in a musician's life
story.community_name: Church, faith and jazz: the sacred and the secular

blocks.x: changes in religion, the idea of churches representing intercession between man and God, that’s got to go. The churches are finished. I think this is the end, in this century, of all churches, including the Roman Catholic church.
That’s an interesting comment, because you, yourself, I remember when we last spoke, it was almost five years ago, you described yourself as a very spiritual person.
But it’s not something that you need the church for.

Well I grew up in the church. I grew up in the African Methodist Episcopal church. But I watched the church abuse my father you know. They worked him until he dropped dead. They didn’t reward him for the work that he did, they just used him to build up other churches then they would award these other churches that he had built up to others who had done nothing. It’s like our political system, like a business promotional system. And I watched all this. And so I realized that churches represent the intercession between the spirit of man and the force that created him, which we may call God or we can call it Allah or we can it Brahmin or Vishnu or whatever name we give it. It’s that force that created us. Because show me a man that made me a man and then I’ll worship him. But until then I will worship He who made man. And so it is that force that the church tries to pretend to be and never is. So the whole system has got to change. You have to fall on your knees and speak to God yourself. Each of us has to become a priest and be his own church, and morally lift ourselves up so we don’t think of doing harm to anybody else. Harm comes first from thought you know. You think of doing harm to someone, then you do something. But if you think about yourself and about who you are and your place in the world, you’re not going to do anybody any harm.
